evals.name: check-reports-each-value-with-its-provenance
evals.prompt: /user-interface:setup check — docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml sets css.important: utilities-only and css.rules.disable: [hover]; docs/conventions/user-interface.local.yaml sets css.token_fallback: literal. No css_* plugin option has a stored value.
evals.expected_output: Writes the userConfig values to a JSON file with the Write tool, runs detect.mjs --config --user-config with that file, and presents one row per css key with its value and provenance: css.important from team, css.token_fallback from local, css.rules.disable from defaults and team, the rest from defaults or userConfig. With no css_* option stored, no key shows userConfig provenance, and no literal ${user_config...} placeholder is written into the userConfig JSON. Writes no config file.
expectations: Runs detect.mjs with --config rather than reading the YAML files and merging them by hand
Passes the userConfig values through a file written with the Write tool, not on a shell command line
Shows each css key's value with its provenance layer (team, local, defaults or userConfig)
Names both defaults and team as the provenance of css.rules.disable
Reports css.important and css.token_fallback provenance as their file or defaults layer, never userConfig, when no css_* option is stored
Leaves out of the userConfig JSON any key whose value is empty or a literal ${user_config...} placeholder
Does not write or edit any config file

evals.name: check-warns-when-worktree-lacks-the-main-checkout-local-file
evals.prompt: /user-interface:setup check — this is a linked worktree. The main checkout (first entry of git worktree list --porcelain) has docs/conventions/user-interface.local.yaml; this worktree has no user-interface.local.* file.
evals.expected_output: The table carries a WARN that this worktree has no personal user-interface.local file while the main checkout has one, explains the file is gitignored so a new worktree does not carry it, and offers to copy it. Nothing is copied during check.
expectations: Identifies the main checkout from the first entry of git worktree list --porcelain
Reports a WARN that the worktree lacks the personal .local file the main checkout has
Says the file is gitignored, which is why the worktree lacks it
Offers to copy the file but does not copy it during check

evals.name: apply-writes-one-key-in-the-team-file
evals.prompt: /user-interface:setup apply css.important=allow — docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml exists with version: 1 and css.token_fallback: propose-token, plus a comment line.
evals.expected_output: Runs check, writes only css.important: allow into the team file in block style, keeps css.token_fallback and the comment, re-runs check and reports css.important = allow with provenance team from the new table.
expectations: Writes css.important: allow in docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml and changes no other key
Keeps the existing comment and css.token_fallback
Uses block-style YAML, no flow mapping
Re-runs check and reports the stored value with provenance team

evals.name: check-reports-broken-convention-home
evals.prompt: /user-interface:setup check — detect.mjs --config returns config.home null and config.home_error saying the convention home is unresolved.
evals.expected_output: A FAIL row says the convention-home pointer line is broken, so the team and personal layers were not read, and points at fixing the pointer line; the skill does not fall back to docs/conventions.
expectations: Reports home_error as a FAIL
Says the team and personal layers were not read
Does not read or write docs/conventions/user-interface.yaml as a fallback

evals.name: apply-userconfig-key-points-at-config
evals.expected_output: Recognizes css_layer as a userConfig option, which this skill does not write, and tells the user to set it through /config or pluginConfigs in user settings and start a fresh session; alternatively offers to write css.layer: components to the user-global file instead.
expectations: Does not edit settings.json itself
Names /config (or pluginConfigs in user settings) as where the userConfig value is set
Offers css.layer in the user-global file as the file-layer alternative
